course.title: Tailwind CSS — From Beginner to Professional Practice
course.description: A visual-first, hands-on course covering the full Tailwind CSS curriculum from HTML/CSS foundations and utility classes to responsive layouts, state variants, design tokens, component integration, accessibility, debugging, performance, production workflows, and v3-to-v4 migration.
course.version_scope: Tailwind CSS v4-first; official documentation checked 2026-10-19. Tailwind CSS v3 migration and maintenance are treated as a separate legacy/optional track.
prerequisites: Basic HTML and CSS are recommended: elements and attributes, CSS selectors, the box model and basic layout. JavaScript and a frontend framework are optional for introductory modules.
Basic command-line and package-manager familiarity is helpful for installation and build workflows.
learning_outcomes: Explain utility-first CSS and the path from source classes to generated CSS.
Set up Tailwind CSS v4 with supported Vite, CLI, PostCSS or framework-specific integration instructions.
Build responsive, readable interfaces with layout, spacing, typography, color, visual effects, state and animation utilities.
Use theme variables, custom utilities and directives to maintain a coherent design system.
Integrate Tailwind with component frameworks and external/shared UI packages using correct source detection.
Review keyboard usability, focus visibility, form semantics, reduced motion and color contrast.
Diagnose missing or conflicting styles, test generated CSS, prepare a production build and reason about v3-to-v4 migration.

learning_roadmap.title: Foundations
learning_roadmap.checkpoint: Create a working page and explain how source utility tokens produce styles.

learning_roadmap.title: Core styling
learning_roadmap.checkpoint: Recreate a product grid and responsive page section with a consistent visual rhythm.

learning_roadmap.title: Responsive and interactive design
learning_roadmap.checkpoint: Build a responsive interface with usable navigation, form states and keyboard feedback.

learning_roadmap.title: Customization and architecture
learning_roadmap.checkpoint: Build a consistent button, card and form pattern using shared tokens.

learning_roadmap.title: Professional development
learning_roadmap.checkpoint: Produce a tested and documented build; treat migration as a separate track.

learning_roadmap.title: Advanced practice
learning_roadmap.checkpoint: Deliver the capstone with accessibility, responsive, build and visual regression checks.

track_policy.core: Modules 1–19 provide the core learning path.
track_policy.legacy_optional: Module 20 covers Tailwind v3 maintenance and v4 migration.
track_policy.advanced_optional: Module 21 contains specialization and professional workflow topics.
